trigger: Impermissible acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI
deadline: Before deciding not to notify; document as soon as the scope is known
notify: Internal decision log (no external recipient)
clock_starts: Presumed a breach unless the assessment shows low probability of compromise
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual by first-class mail (email if agreed); substitute notice if contact information is out of date (10 or more: 90-day website posting or major media plus a toll-free number active at least 90 days)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach involving 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with the individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach involving fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: No later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year of discovery
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
clock_starts: End of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered

trigger: Breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 residents of Florida (or of any other state)
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with the Director of Marketing and Communications

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
notify: Hold notices; record the official's identity and statement in the decision log

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A business associate (for example the clearinghouse, MSSP, EHR vendor) discovers a breach of company PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the BA's discovery; Tier 1 BAAs are moving to 5 business days (STD-03)
notify: The company (Compliance and Privacy Officer), with identities of affected individuals
clock_starts: BA's discovery (164.410(a)(2)); the company's own clock may start earlier if the BA is its agent (164.404(a)(2))

trigger: Any impermissible use or disclosure
deadline: Keep documentation for 6 years
notify: Internal records

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical history or treatment and health insurance identifiers) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; a notice made under HIPAA is deemed compliant if the company timely provides a copy of it to the Department of Legal Affairs
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm the deemed-compliance path with counsel; notice may be delayed on a written law enforcement request (501.171(4)(b))
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent maintaining personal information for the company has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days following the agent's determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: The company (Compliance and Privacy Officer)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the affected list by state of residence

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any consideration of a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Voluntary law enforcement and CISA report
citation: OFAC advisory (2021-09-21) mitigating factor; FBI IC3 and CISA reporting guidance
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practical (target within 48 hours)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck applicability when final

trigger: Suspected security incident or vendor outage that may lead to a claim
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging incident response vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline; broker

trigger: Security incident or outage affecting joint venture patients, data, or services
deadline: Per agreement: within 72 hours of confirming a security incident, and prompt notice of service outages
notify: Joint venture partner's designated security and compliance contacts

trigger: Severity 1 incident or material disruption
deadline: Per credit agreement; sponsor operating partner informed within 24 hours (internal rule)
notify: Lender agent (if the agreement requires); sponsor operating partner; audit committee chair

obligation: FDA medical device report by a device user facility
trigger: Information reasonably suggests a device (including a compromised or malfunctioning networked device, or AI-003 software) caused or contributed to a patient death or serious injury at the ASC or imaging center
deadline: No more than 10 work days after becoming aware
notify: Death: FDA and the manufacturer. Serious injury: the manufacturer (FDA if the manufacturer is unknown)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the ASC (ambulatory surgical facility) and the imaging center (outpatient diagnostic facility) are device user facilities; clinics are physician offices and are excluded
owner: ASC Administrator or Imaging Center Director with the Chief Medical Officer

trigger: Breach of SUD treatment records from a Part 2 program
deadline: Same as HIPAA
notify: Patients, HHS, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company does not operate a federally assisted SUD program

trigger: Breach of PHR identifiable health information by a non-HIPAA vendor
deadline: n/a
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is a HIPAA covered entity (318.1 excludes covered entities acting as such)
